title: Trying the recent image to animating animal workflow idea - almost there ! Would love to hear ideas.
author: ogimaru

comments.author: ogimaru
comments.body:
Just a small update to the experiment; It turns out even without a lora, H3 does a pretty nice job if its done simultaneously. Here we see the drawbacks of only sideview, and how much better we can get with multiview 

https://reddit.com/link/pgl9w8c/video/vsulbncaqbvh1/player

It does struggle at times to get all limbs colored accurately in some parts -- but looks good enough for now.

replies.author: Ok-Director4174
replies.body:
Nice progress. Since H3 does better when the views are generated together, you could push that one step earlier: have Qwen-Image 2.1 (edit mode, with the side-view image as reference) make a single multi-view sheet of the same animal, e.g. "the same bear from the image, shown three times side by side: side view, front view, three-quarter view, same pose, plain gray background". In edit mode it keeps the identity across views quite well (fur pattern, proportions). Then use that sheet as the first frame, so H3 animates all the views in one video and they stay in sync by construction, instead of trying to sync separate videos afterwards.

Two things that helped me with Qwen-Image 2.1 for this kind of sheet: list explicitly what must stay identical, and keep the background plain and identical for each view, so cropping the views out later is trivial.

If it's useful: I'm doing something similar on the image side (Qwen-Image 2.1 through stable-diffusion.cpp in a native app, Vulkan/CUDA/Metal, automatic VRAM/RAM split so it fits 12 GB). It's open source if you want to borrow anything: [https://github.com/GabrieleLozupone/kokon](https://github.com/GabrieleLozupone/kokon) (measured backend numbers in docs/engineering-notes.md)
